peptide.name: Retatrutide
peptide.summary: Retatrutide is an investigational triple hormone receptor agonist, developed by Eli Lilly, that simultaneously activates the GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors. It produced the largest pharmacological weight loss recorded to date in a phase 2 trial (24.2% at 48 weeks). It is NOT yet FDA-approved -- it remains in phase 3 (the TRIUMPH program) as of this review, and claims of approval circulating in some vendor/marketing material are inaccurate.
peptide.description: Retatrutide (LY3437943) is a synthetic ~39-amino-acid peptide built on a GIP receptor agonist backbone, engineered to also activate the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, making it the first-in-class 'triple G' (GIP/GLP-1/glucagon) agonist. It binds human GCGR, GIPR, and GLP-1R with reported EC50 values of 5.79, 0.0643, and 0.775 nM respectively. Unlike dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists such as tirzepatide, the added glucagon receptor activity contributes a thermogenic and energy-expenditure component: despite glucagon receptor activation normally raising blood glucose, retatrutide produces net glucose lowering because the GLP-1 and GIP effects predominate. A phase 2 trial (NEJM 2023) reported up to 24.2% mean body weight loss at 48 weeks (12 mg dose) -- the most substantial pharmacological weight loss recorded to date, with weight curves still declining at study end; newer 68-week data have reported up to 28.7% loss at the highest dose. As of this review, retatrutide is still completing phase 3 trials (the TRIUMPH program) and has NOT received FDA approval; some vendor/marketing sources inaccurately state it is FDA-approved, which should be disregarded.
peptide.mechanism_of_action: Simultaneous agonist at three G-protein-coupled receptors: the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR), the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R), and the glucagon receptor (GCGR). GLP-1R activity slows gastric emptying, enhances satiety, and reduces appetite; GIPR activity enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion and supports beta-cell function; GCGR activity adds a thermogenic, energy-expenditure-raising component not present in dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists. The combined GLP-1/GIP insulinotropic effect outweighs glucagon's glucose-raising tendency, producing net glucose lowering.

half_life.note: Approximately 6 days, consistent with once-weekly dosing used in trials; based on the same fatty-diacid albumin-binding strategy as tirzepatide.

peptide.evidence_note: Phase 1b (Lancet 2022) and phase 2 (NEJM 2023) trials have been published showing dose-dependent weight loss and glycemic effects, with phase 2 producing the largest recorded pharmacological weight loss (24.2% at 48 weeks). Phase 3 (TRIUMPH program) is ongoing as of this review. No long-term post-marketing safety data exist because the drug is not yet approved.
peptide.fda_status_note: NOT FDA-approved. As of this review, retatrutide remains in phase 3 clinical trials (the TRIUMPH program); some marketing/vendor sources have inaccurately claimed FDA approval, which should be disregarded pending an actual regulatory decision. Verify current status against FDA/Lilly announcements before relying on this for decisions.
peptide.compounding_note: Not an FDA-approved drug; not on the 503A bulks list; not eligible for legal pharmacy compounding while investigational. (Compounding of GLP-1-class drugs more broadly has been a distinct, evolving regulatory area -- verify current status separately.)

benefits.label: Substantial weight loss (phase 2)
benefits.detail: Up to 24.2% mean body weight loss at 48 weeks (12 mg dose) in the phase 2 trial, the largest pharmacological weight loss recorded to date; newer 68-week data report up to 28.7% at the highest dose.

benefits.label: Net glucose lowering despite glucagon agonism
benefits.detail: GLP-1/GIP insulinotropic effects outweigh glucagon's glucose-raising tendency, producing net glycemic improvement in trials.

benefits.label: Added energy-expenditure component (mechanistic)
benefits.detail: Glucagon receptor activation is proposed to add a thermogenic/energy-expenditure effect beyond dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists in preclinical obese-mouse models.

risks.label: No long-term post-marketing safety data
risks.detail: As an investigational, not-yet-approved drug, long-term real-world safety data do not yet exist.

risks.label: GI tolerability
risks.detail: GI side effects common to incretin-class drugs (nausea, diarrhea, vomiting) have been reported in trials, generally dose-dependent.

risks.label: Unregulated 'research chemical' sourcing
risks.detail: Because it is not yet approved, any retatrutide obtained outside a clinical trial is unregulated research-grade material, not a pharmaceutical product.

contraindications.label: Personal/family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2
contraindications.detail: Class-wide theoretical concern shared with other incretin-mimetic drugs pending retatrutide-specific labeling.

interactions.effect: Class-wide concern for increased hypoglycemia risk when combined with other glucose-lowering agents.

reconstitution.note: In trials, supplied as a ready-to-use solution for subcutaneous injection. Research-grade lyophilized powder (outside trial settings) would be reconstituted with bacteriostatic water; concentration depends on diluent volume.

lyophilized.stability: Stable when kept cold and dry (research-grade material).

reconstituted.stability: Refrigerate; use within a limited window.

peptide.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. Retatrutide is NOT FDA-approved as of this review and remains investigational (phase 3). Disregard any marketing claims of approval and verify current status independently. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.

dose_ranges.context: Phase 2 obesity trial (NEJM 2023) — investigational, not an approved dose
dose_ranges.note: Phase 2 trial tested doses from 1 mg up to 12 mg weekly with dose-dependent weight loss (up to 24.2% at 48 weeks with 12 mg). This reflects a clinical trial design, not an approved or recommended dose for individual use.

protocols.name: Dose-escalation schedule (phase 2/3 trial pattern)
protocols.description: Published trials titrate retatrutide upward over several weeks to the target dose to manage GI tolerability, similar to other incretin-class drugs. Summarized from trial design; not an approved regimen since the drug remains investigational.
protocols.cycling_notes: Chronic therapy pattern in trials, not cycled. No approved regimen exists outside clinical trials.
protocols.disclaimer: Summary of clinical trial design for educational reference. Not medical advice; not an approved dosing regimen.

related.note: Both are Lilly-developed multi-receptor incretin agonists; tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist, while retatrutide adds glucagon receptor agonism as a triple agonist.
Both are incretin-based metabolic therapies, though semaglutide is a single GLP-1 receptor agonist versus retatrutide's triple-receptor mechanism.

Both are multi-receptor incretin/glucagon agonists in active development; mazdutide is a dual GLP-1/glucagon agonist while retatrutide adds GIP receptor agonism. No head-to-head trial exists between them.
